name: Markus Persson
category: Video game programmer and designer (Minecraft / Mojang)
milestone_by_age_26: By ~2003 at age 23–24, co-founded development of Wurm Online (public alpha 2003; commercial release 2006) with Rolf Jansson via Mojang Specifications—his first shipped commercial MMO sandbox game before Minecraft.
early_history_summary: Born in Stockholm (1979) to a railroad-worker father and nurse mother; programmed on a Commodore 128 from age ~7 and made a text adventure at 8. After incomplete high school and graphic-design study, he worked as a web designer and at King (Midasplayer) while co-building Wurm Online (2002–2007), then released Minecraft Classic in May 2009 at age 29.
family_context_summary: Parents divorced when he was ~7; periods of food insecurity; father (later deceased by suicide) was a hobbyist nerd who taught him the family Commodore 128; mother a nurse.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father transferred early computer access and nerd culture rather than a commercial game-industry apprenticeship; no elite industry network documented.
primary_early_advantage_tags: childhood programming, Wurm Online, indie TIGSource community, King browser-game job, Minecraft
evidence_summary: Persson’s ≤26 milestone is co-creating Wurm Online (alpha 2003, release 2006) with Jansson under Mojang Specifications—dated via Wikipedia and Wurm/Minecraft histories—before Minecraft’s May 2009 public release at age 29 made him globally famous. Early Commodore access and years of game programming plus online indie feedback compound product taste; family finances were constrained after divorce rather than a safety net. Later Microsoft’s $2.5B Mojang acquisition cemented tier-1 status.
starting_point: Born in Stockholm (1979) to a Finnish nurse mother and Swedish railroad-worker father; grew up partly in Edsbyn with early home-computer access after parents’ divorce and financial strain.
current_position: Billionaire Minecraft creator (Notch); left Mojang after Microsoft’s 2014 acquisition; runs Bitshift Entertainment / personal projects; polarizing public figure; net worth on order of ~$1B+.

trajectory.event: Wurm Online entered public alpha; co-developed with Rolf Jansson as first major commercial game project under Mojang Specifications.
Wurm Online commercially released; Persson continued as co-creator before exiting the project in late 2007.
Released Minecraft Classic on TIGSource (17 May 2009), beginning the breakout that made the game history’s best-seller.
Left jAlbum to work full-time on Minecraft as Alpha success accelerated; later declined a Valve job offer.
Minecraft full release and first Minecon; handed lead design to Jens Bergensten.
Microsoft acquired Mojang for $2.5B; Persson left and became a billionaire.
Relaunched post-Mojang studio efforts as Bitshift Entertainment, teeing new game projects.

name: Greg Gianforte
category: Software entrepreneur and politician (RightNow / Montana governor)
milestone_by_age_26: In 1986 at age ~24–25, co-founded Brightwork Development Inc. (LAN management software) in New Jersey after leaving Bell Labs; served as president for eight years until a ~$10M McAfee sale in 1994.
early_history_summary: Born San Diego (1961), raised in Philadelphia suburbs; high-school class president and early software tinkerer. Earned BE EE + MS CS from Stevens Institute (1983), worked at Bell Labs, then left bureaucracy to co-found Brightwork (1986). Later founded RightNow Technologies in Bozeman (1997), sold to Oracle for ~$1.5B (2011), then entered politics as U.S. Representative and Montana governor.
family_context_summary: Father Frank was an aerospace engineer (later landlord); mother Dale worked at General Dynamics then taught math; raised in relatively affluent King of Prussia / Wayne area after early San Diego years.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father’s engineering career and Stevens alma mater path gave domain-adjacent modeling; not a software-product apprenticeship per se.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Stevens engineering, Bell Labs, Brightwork founding, bootstrapping, RightNow CRM
evidence_summary: Inc. Magazine and governor bios date Brightwork’s 1986 founding when Gianforte was ~25, with an eight-year presidency ending in the 1994 McAfee sale—clear ≤26 material founder milestone corroborated by Wikipedia. Engineering family, Stevens degrees, and Bell Labs provided a technical launchpad without inherited capital markets access. RightNow’s later IPO and Oracle sale, then Montana governorship, define tier-3 public/tech impact.
starting_point: Born in San Diego (1961) to an aerospace-engineer father and math-teacher/General Dynamics mother; raised in affluent Philadelphia suburbs and followed father to Stevens Institute.
current_position: 25th Governor of Montana (since 2021; reelected 2024); former U.S. Representative; software fortune from RightNow/Oracle sale.

trajectory.event: Co-founded Brightwork Development (LAN management software) and became president after leaving Bell Labs.
Sold Brightwork to McAfee for about $10 million; briefly led North American sales.
Co-founded RightNow Technologies with wife Susan in Bozeman, building cloud CRM.
RightNow went public with 1,000+ employees worldwide.
Oracle acquired RightNow for about $1.5 billion.
Won Montana’s at-large U.S. House special election (later pled guilty to misdemeanor assault of a reporter).
Inaugurated as Governor of Montana; reelected in 2024.

name: Zhang Yiming
milestone_by_age_26: In 2009 at age 26, founded 99fang.com (real-estate search), his first company, after taking over Kuxun’s real-estate vertical when Expedia was acquiring Kuxun—material first founding before ByteDance (2012, age 28–29).
early_history_summary: Born Longyan, Fujian (1983) to civil-servant parents; Nankai University computer engineering BEng (2005). First engineer/fifth employee at travel site Kuxun (2006), briefly Microsoft and Fanfou, then founded 99fang (2009). Left to found ByteDance with Liang Rubo (March 2012), launching Toutiao then Douyin/TikTok.
family_context_summary: Only son of civil-servant parents in Longyan, Fujian; middle-class public-sector household rather than tech-wealth dynasty.
parent_family_domain_summary: Parents were civil servants; no documented software/internet entrepreneurship transfer.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Nankai engineering, Kuxun early hire, 99fang founding, mobile recommendation wave, ByteDance
evidence_summary: Wikipedia, Bloomberg, and LinkedIn date 99fang founding to 2009 when Zhang was 26—his first company and a dated ≤26 founder milestone—before ByteDance (2012) at 28–29 drove legendary wealth via Toutiao/TikTok. Civil-servant family and Nankai engineering provided competence without capital inheritance; mobile content and AI recs were the later structural wave. Stepped down as ByteDance CEO/chair around 2021 while retaining major voting control.
starting_point: Born 1983 in Longyan, Fujian, as only son of civil servants; studied microelectronics/software at Nankai University in Tianjin.
current_position: ByteDance founder and major voting-control shareholder after stepping down as CEO/chair (2021); among the world’s richest people via TikTok/Douyin parent (~$90B+ class fortune).

trajectory.event: Joined Kuxun as fifth employee and first engineer; later became technical director.
Founded 99fang.com real-estate search, spinning out Kuxun’s property vertical as Expedia acquired the parent.
Co-founded ByteDance with Liang Rubo; launched Toutiao news aggregator.
Launched TikTok internationally; Douyin already scaling in China.
ByteDance acquired Musical.ly for ~$800M and merged into TikTok; company valued as top private startup.
Stepped down as ByteDance CEO/chair while retaining majority voting rights.

early_history_summary: Born Boston 1927 to Irish and Lithuanian Jewish immigrant parents; self-taught college math, Caltech BS, Princeton PhD; AI field-founding and Lisp came in late 20s/30s.
family_context_summary: Immigrant parents (Irish father, Lithuanian Jewish mother); family moved frequently in Depression until father organized for Amalgamated Clothing Workers in LA; both parents active Communists in the 1930s.
parent_family_domain_summary: Parents encouraged learning/critical thinking but were not computer-science professionals (field barely existed).

name: Scott Chacon
category: Software entrepreneur (GitHub cofounder; Pro Git author)
milestone_by_age_26: In 2007–2008 at age ~25–26, co-founded GitHub with Tom Preston-Werner, Chris Wanstrath, and P.J. Hyett; platform development began Oct 2007 and launched 2008, establishing him as a core founding engineer/operator of the dominant Git hosting company.
early_history_summary: Git evangelist who became known as the local 'Git guy' in Ruby meetups before joining the founding team that built GitHub (2007–2008). Authored the canonical Pro Git book (Apress; free at git-scm.com), helped scale GitHub from four founders to hundreds of employees before Microsoft’s $7.5B acquisition, later cofounded Chatterbug and GitButler.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Git expertise, Ruby community, GitHub cofounders, Pro Git distribution, open-source wave
evidence_summary: Wikipedia and GitHub histories list Chacon among the four founders who launched GitHub in 2008; with curated birth year 1982 that is age ~25–26—qualifying cofounder milestone with multi-source corroboration. Git teaching (Pro Git) and cofounder team were primary levers on the structural Git/social-coding wave. Family background is undocumented; later Microsoft acquisition and GitButler continue the version-control thread.
starting_point: Not documented in reviewed sources beyond early identity as a Git-focused Ruby/open-source developer who met cofounders via local meetups.
current_position: Cofounder/CEO of GitButler (Berlin); former GitHub cofounder; author of Pro Git; also known for Chatterbug and open-source advocacy.

trajectory.event: GitHub launched with Chacon as one of four cofounders after 2007 development; became core product/Git evangelist.
Published Pro Git (Apress), which became the canonical free Git textbook at git-scm.com.
Cofounded language-learning company Chatterbug after GitHub tenure.
Microsoft acquired GitHub for $7.5 billion after the company scaled to hundreds of employees.
Cofounded GitButler to rethink version control UX for modern (and AI-assisted) workflows.

name: Geert Uytterhoeven
milestone_by_age_26: By 1994 at age ~23, was an active Linux/m68k kernel hacker (Amiga port lineage—the first non-Intel Linux port), running linux-m68k.org-era work, meeting Linus Torvalds at a Belgian conference, and contributing patches recognized in the kernel community.
early_history_summary: Born/raised Leuven, Belgium (~1971). Learned BASIC from TV then Commodore 64/Amiga assembler; entered Linux via Amiga 4000. By 23 (1994) deeply involved in m68k port and student networking (Kotnet at KU Leuven); later PhD in wavelets (defended 1999) while remaining a long-term kernel maintainer; day job embedded systems (e.g., Sony SDCE).
family_context_summary: Born, raised, and based in Leuven, Belgium; used parents’ car to pick up Torvalds in 1994—family supportive but not a tech dynasty in reviewed sources.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Amiga/m68k, early Linux port, Torvalds network, KU Leuven, kernel maintainership
evidence_summary: Linux.com profile (2001) states he was 23 in 1994 and already a multi-year programmer deeply in Linux/m68k, meeting Torvalds that year—corroborated by LinkedIn linux-m68k.org activity from Mar 1994. Early home computers plus open-source email culture created scarce architecture skill on the first non-x86 Linux port. Career sustained as long-term maintainer and embedded engineer rather than celebrity founder (tier-3 specialist).
starting_point: Born and raised in Leuven, Belgium; self-taught programmer via Belgian TV BASIC, Commodore 64, then Amiga systems that led into Linux.
current_position: Long-time Linux kernel contributor/maintainer (m68k and related areas); embedded Linux technologist (Glider / industry roles); active for 30+ years in the kernel community.

trajectory.event: Active Linux/m68k kernel contributor; met Linus Torvalds at a small Belgian conference; began PhD era while hacking Amiga Linux.
Defended PhD (wavelets) at KU Leuven while continuing kernel work.
Profiled as key 2.4-era m68k integrator working embedded systems at Sony’s Brussels center.
Continued multi-decade m68k/embedded maintainership listed in professional bios through the 2010s–2020s.
